clue.text: Noblemen poison wine

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or poison something
Graves is a wine from the Bordeaux region of France

explanation.surface: Aristocrats are tampering with the wine by poisoning it.
explanation.definitionFit: A margrave was a German nobleman ranking with a marquis, governing a border province.

clue.text: Joint account's closing in difficult situation

indicators.note: in says the closing letter is placed inside the word for a difficult situation

parts.note: to be in the mire is to be in a difficult situation

indicators.note: closing points to the final letter of the word account

explanation.surface: A shared bank account is wound up while the holders are in financial trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint account' reads as one banking phrase, but 'Joint' alone is the definition; 'account's closing' is T, the last letter of account.
explanation.definitionFit: A mitre joint is the angled corner joint used in carpentry and picture frames.

clue.text: Run out with disgusted expression over players getting plastered

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first pieces above the next one

parts.note: RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out
ugh is an exclamation of disgust
the cast are the players in a production

explanation.surface: A cricketer is run out, grimaces, and the team goes off to get drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plastered' looks like slang for drunk, but here it means coated with plaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Roughcast is a coarse plaster of lime and gravel, so a roughcast wall has been coated with it.

clue.text: Having painful joints, he tucked into drink with a spasm

indicators.note: tucked into says the word he is placed inside the drink

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a drink
a tic is a twitch or spasm

explanation.surface: An aching man downs his rum and suffers a twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheumatism causes pain and stiffness in the joints, so a sufferer is described as rheumatic.

clue.text: English composer Sullivan worked with him, a wag

indicators.note: worked means the letters are worked into a new shape, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Suggests that Arthur Sullivan once collaborated with a joker of a fellow composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked' rearranges SULLIVAN, HIM, A and WAG together.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Vaughan Williams was a leading English composer of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Extremely subtle documentaries broadcast 4's work

indicators.note: extremely asks for the letters at the extremes of the word subtle
broadcast means scattered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some very understated documentaries are aired about a composer's output.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' gives SE, the ends of subtle; 'broadcast' rearranges DOCUMENTARIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Serenade to Music is a 1938 choral piece by Vaughan Williams, the composer at 4 down.

clue.text: Credit card finally found in marketplace on return

indicators.note: on return says the whole assembled word is read backwards
found in says the last letter of card sits inside the marketplace

parts.note: a souk is an Arab marketplace

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word card

explanation.surface: A credit card is lost and then found in a bazaar on the way back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' puts D into SOUK, giving SODUK, and 'on return' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: Kudos is praise or prestige, the credit someone earns for an achievement.

clue.text: Lark Ascending enthrals a South African village

indicators.note: enthrals means holds captive, so the reversed word holds the a inside it
in a down clue, ascending means the word lark is read upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: Vaughan Williams's The Lark Ascending charms a rural South African community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ascending' turns LARK into KRAL, and 'enthrals' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A kraal is a traditional enclosed village of huts in southern Africa.

clue.text: As before, not all recommend it totally

indicators.note: not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A reviewer holds back from fully endorsing something, just as last time.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto means the same again, used to repeat what was said or written previously.

clue.text: Resignation is more certain to involve split

indicators.note: to involve means to take in, so the word for more certain wraps around split

parts.note: surer means more certain
to rend is to split or tear apart

explanation.surface: Quitting is the safer option when a party is about to divide.
explanation.definitionFit: Surrender is giving in, an acceptance of defeat like resignation.

clue.text: Canadian politician impolite in letter to Mitsotakis?

indicators.note: in places the word for impolite inside the Greek letter

parts.note: Mitsotakis is a Greek prime minister, so a letter to him is a Greek letter, here tau
rude means impolite

explanation.surface: A Canadian leader sends a rude letter to the Greek prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'letter to Mitsotakis' is not correspondence but a letter of his alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre and Justin Trudeau both served as Prime Minister of Canada.

clue.text: Clergyman pockets a pile

indicators.note: pockets means takes into itself, so the clergyman word holds the a

parts.note: a rector is a parish clergyman

explanation.surface: A vicar pockets a heap of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pile' suggests a heap or fortune, but it is the old name for an atomic reactor.
explanation.definitionFit: Early nuclear reactors were called atomic piles, after the stacked graphite blocks.

clue.text: Place in Surrey for one needing meat

parts.note: eg, for example, means for one
ham is a meat

explanation.surface: A town in Surrey suits someone craving meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Egham is a town in Surrey, the county south-west of London, home to Royal Holloway university.

clue.text: First off, replace outside toilets and relax

indicators.note: outside says the shortened word goes around the toilets
first off means the opening letter of the word for replace is removed

parts.note: to change is to replace
loos are toilets

explanation.surface: Before anything else, swap the outdoor lavatories and then take it easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First off' drops C from CHANGE, leaving HANGE, which goes 'outside' LOOS.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang loose is an informal idiom for staying calm and taking things easy.

clue.text: At home adult takes exercise, being unfit

parts.note: in means at home
A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult
PT is physical training, exercise

explanation.surface: A grown-up does a workout at home because they are out of shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfit' suggests poor physical condition, but it means unsuitable.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means unsuitable or inappropriate, not fit for the purpose.

clue.text: Dish in Venice, starter of toasted carrot

indicators.note: to dish is to ruin or spoil, so these letters are broken up and rearranged
starter of points to the first letter of the word toasted

explanation.surface: A Venetian recipe begins with toasted carrot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dish' rearranges the letters of Venice plus the first of toasted into CENTIVE. 'carrot' is the reward dangled in front of a donkey, not food.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrot is a reward offered to motivate someone, which is exactly an incentive.

clue.text: Lumpy old bed aunt moved out of bedroom initially

indicators.note: moved means these letters are shifted into a new order
out of says the opening letter of bedroom is taken away from bed
initially points to the first letter of the word bedroom

explanation.surface: An aunt's lumpy old bed has been carried out of the bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' drops B ('bedroom initially') from BED, leaving ED; 'moved' rearranges OLD, ED and AUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodulated means covered in nodules, small knobs or swellings, so lumpy.

clue.text: One may replace Yale lecturer with hick, most foolishly

indicators.note: foolishly means the letters are arranged in a silly new order

explanation.surface: Suggests an American university swapping a professor for the most foolish yokel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yale' looks like the university, but it is the lock brand. 'foolishly' rearranges HICK and MOST.
explanation.definitionFit: Yale is a well-known brand of lock, and fitting or changing locks is a locksmith's trade.

clue.text: Piece of wood that will make 8?

definitions.meaning: a length of timber two inches by four in section
two multiplied by four makes eight

explanation.surface: Asks which bit of timber will produce the number eight.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-by-four is a standard timber size, and two times four equals eight.

clue.text: Religious teacher from Chartres regularly ignored Jesus? Not right

indicators.note: regularly ignored means every other letter of Chartres is dropped, keeping the rest
not says the abbreviation for right is removed from the saviour's title

parts.note: Christ is the title of Jesus

explanation.surface: A cathedral teacher in Chartres skips services and denies Jesus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly ignored' keeps C, A, T, E from Chartres; 'Not right' removes R from CHRIST, leaving CHIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A catechist teaches the principles of Christian faith by question and answer.

clue.text: Singers from church knocked back port

indicators.note: knocked back means the port's name is read in reverse

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: Choristers leave church and down a glass of port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like drinking port, but it reverses RIO, the port city.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir is a group of singers, usually in a church.

clue.text: Expert breaks into stately mansion at first? That's easy

indicators.note: breaks into says the expert word goes inside the word for stately

parts.note: noble means stately or grand
a pro is an expert

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word mansion

explanation.surface: A professional burglar breaks into a stately home and finds it a doddle.
explanation.definitionFit: No problem is an informal reply meaning something is simple to do.

clue.text: Father and daughter kept in trim

indicators.note: kept in says the daughter's letter is held inside the word for trim

parts.note: to pare is to trim

explanation.surface: Dad and his daughter both keep fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trim' reads as an adjective for slim, but it is the verb pare.
explanation.definitionFit: Padre is a title for a priest, especially a military chaplain, addressed as Father.

clue.text: Love role displaying creative style

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
a part is a role in a play

explanation.surface: A romantic part lets an actor show off their artistic flair.
explanation.definitionFit: Op art is a 1960s art movement using optical illusions, a style of creative work.

clue.text: One's driven up river on island

indicators.note: in an across clue, on places the river after the island

parts.note: Skye is a Scottish island

explanation.surface: Someone is chauffeured up the river on a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driven' suggests a car, but in cricket a ball is driven, and one hit high into the air is a skyer.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a skyer is a mishit that goes high up into the air.

clue.text: Once more offend Amber?

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again, once more
to sin is to offend or transgress

explanation.surface: Asks whether a woman called Amber has transgressed again.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks Amber as an example of the answer: amber is a fossilised resin.
explanation.definitionFit: Amber is fossilised tree resin, so it is one example of the definition.

clue.text: State aid put back into local area

indicators.note: into says the reversed word goes inside the pub

parts.note: a local is a pub, an inn

indicators.note: put back means the word aid is written backwards

explanation.surface: State funding is returned to the local district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' looks like an adjective but is the noun meaning a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is one of the fifty states of the USA.

clue.text: Smart outfits inlaid with gold will get admirers

indicators.note: inlaid with says the gold is set into the outfits word

parts.note: suits are smart outfits
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Dapper clothes trimmed with gold will attract fans.
explanation.definitionFit: Suitors are men who court a woman, so they are her admirers.

clue.text: Build playground in vacated establishment

indicators.note: in says the playground word goes inside the emptied word
vacated means emptied, so only the outer letters of establishment remain

parts.note: a rec, short for recreation ground, is a playground

explanation.surface: A play area is built on the site of a closed-down business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacated' empties establishment to ET, and REC goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: To erect is to construct or put up a structure.

clue.text: Bag with tea in, and sweetener

parts.note: a sac is a bag or pouch
char is informal British slang for tea

explanation.surface: A teabag goes in, and then the artificial sweetener.
explanation.definitionFit: Saccharin is an artificial substance used in place of sugar.
